wins: Completed initial TCP SYN scan across the /24 target range and identified ports 22/80/445, providing a clear attack surface for follow-on work.
Captured service banners from SSH and HTTP services, yielding high-confidence context for subsequent fingerprinting.
fails: Unable to achieve lateral movement or privilege escalation, leaving the mission objective incomplete despite detailed reconnaissance.
Repeatedly failed to authenticate to SMB shares due to missing credentials, preventing data extraction.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase executed effectively (scans and banner grabs) but the campaign stalled during credential-based access, resulting in zero mission success.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Authentication attempts to SMB/SSH services were made without validated credentials, leading to consistent denial responses.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 80/443 is open and HTTP banner indicates CMS software
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted web enumeration with dirsearch and CMS-specific scripts

skill_cards.if_condition: When SSH port 22 is reachable and banner shows OpenSSH
skill_cards.then_action: Execute automated SSH enumeration (ssh-audit + nmap ssh-* scripts)

skill_cards.if_condition: When SMB port 445 responds with a valid session response
skill_cards.then_action: Use smbclient with anonymous and credential lists to enumerate shares and pull smb.conf

memory_ops.reason: High-value web enumeration consistently followed initial HTTP discovery.

next_experiments.title: Credential Harvesting and Reuse
next_experiments.description: Investigate pivot points from captured HTTP/SSH banners (look for default creds or API keys) and feed them into SMB/SSH login attempts to overcome the authentication failure pattern.

next_experiments.title: SMB Share Validation with Alternative Tools
next_experiments.description: Switch to CrackMapExec/enum4linux with built-in credential spraying and share enumeration to validate SMB access paths skipped by smbclient.

next_experiments.title: OSCP-style Posture Verification
next_experiments.description: Use automated scripts (e.g., BloodHound + SharpHound collection) against enumerated services to map trust relationships before attempting lateral traversal.
